content:
Dog & Puppy Vaccination Schedule – Complete Guide

As a dog parent, there’s nothing more devastating than losing your furry friend to a preventable disease. However, it’s really a heart sinking view to see your once energetic and playful companion succumb to debilitating illness. Many of the pet parents forget about dog vaccination dates and have gone through this heartbreak. Not only this, but every year, thousands of dogs lose their life to dangerous diseases which could be prevented with proper vaccination shots.

With this post, we are going to explain everything related to dog & puppy vaccination schedule for every life stage, which includes importance of vaccine, different types of vaccines available, vaccination schedule chart, vaccines side effects, and many other important points so follow this article till the end.

Table of Contents

  • Why Do I Vaccinate My Dog?
  • Types of Dog Vaccine & What Diseases Do Vaccines Prevent?
  • An Ideal Puppy Vaccination Schedule for All Breeds in India
  • Mandatory Vaccination Schedule for Adult Dogs in India
  • Which Dog Vaccines Does My Dog Need?
  • Don’t Let Your Dog Suffer: The Importance of Vaccinations
  • Factors to Keep in Mind While Dog Vaccinations
  • How Do I Know My Dog Is Up To Date on Shots?
  • What is The Dog Vaccination Price in India?
  • How Safe Are Dog Vaccines?
  • Dog Vaccination Side Effects: What You Need to Know
  • What to do When Your Dog Experience Side Effects?
  • FAQ’s About Dog & Puppy Vaccination Schedule

Why Do I Vaccinate My Dog?

It is really important to vaccinate your dog on time. However, there are many of the reasons why:

Prevents deadly disease: Vaccines are really helpful for your dogs to fight off with deadly diseases.

Reduces risk of transmission: When you follow proper dog vaccination schedule then they less likely to transmit diseases to other dogs and even humans.

Saves lives: Vaccination works wonders for dogs. However, they work to reduce the mortality rate of dogs from preventable diseases.

Protect public health: When you follow on time puppy vaccination schedule then you are not just protecting your dog but overall public health. Vaccination helps to reduce the risk of zoonotic diseases. Zoonotic diseases are the type of diseases that can be transmitted from animals to humans.

Types of Dog Vaccine & What Diseases Do Vaccines Prevent?

There are two main types of vaccine available for dogs. Here are both of them:

1. Core Vaccine

Core vaccines are essential for all dogs irrespective of their lifestyle or location. These vaccines are helpful to prevent your dog from:

  • Rabies: This is fatal viral disease which affects the nervous system of your four legged friend.
  • Distemper: The next up disease is contagious and often fatal viral disease which directly affects on respiratory, gastrointestinal, and nervous systems.
  • Hepatitis: Hepatitis is actually a viral disease which affects on liver and even they can cause fever, vomiting and diarrhea.
  • Parvovirus: This is a highly contagious and potentially life threatening viral disease which affects on gastrointestinal system.

2. Non-Core Vaccine

Non-core vaccines are actually recommended for dogs as per their lifestyle, location and risk of exposure. These vaccines are really helpful to fight with:

  • Bordetella: This is a bacterial disease which affects on respiratory system and is commonly known as kennel cough.
  • Leptospirosis: This is also a bacterial disease which affects the kidney and liver. The disease also gets transmitted through contamination of water and soil.
  • Lyme Disease: The next up also have a bacterial disease which is famous to attack the joints and is transmission through back bites.
  • Coronavirus: Canine coronavirus although it’s not usually life-threatening by itself, canine coronavirus can lead to some tummy troubles for our furry friends and might sometimes result in more serious issues like viral hemorrhagic disease.

Just a friendly reminder: This virus does not affect humans it’s only affects dogs and not related COVID-19 or SARS-COV2.

The only way to protect your furry friend from this virus is to vaccinate on time. Your nearby veterinary doctor in Delhi can recommend which non-core vaccines are suitable for your dog based on its individual risk profile.

Shots for dogs schedule is one of the most important part of dog’s health and wellbeing. When correctly understand the type of dog vaccines and diseases that they prevent then you can make a wise choice about their shots. Also, not forget that vaccination is such an important step to prevent your dog from deadly disease to ensure their health and long life.

The Devastating Reality of Unvaccinated Dogs: Protect Your Furry Friend Today with Our At-home Vaccination Services.

The next section of our post is going to help you get detailed knowledge about proper vaccination schedule of dogs in India, what type of vaccination does your pet needs and other important points. Let’s get started.

An Ideal Puppy Vaccination Schedule for All Breeds in India

One of the most vulnerable time of a dog life is it’s new born or puppy days. This is exactly first few months of their life. In order to protect them, there is a series of vaccination that recommended at specific interval. Here are the details of puppy shot schedule:

  • 6-8 weeks: When your puppy is 6-8 weeks old, you need to vaccinate them with Distemper, Hepatitis, Parvovirus (DHPP).
  • 10-12 weeks: as your puppy grows and is 10-12 weeks old, you have to vaccinate them with DHPP and Parainfluenza.
  • 14-16 weeks: The period of 14-16 weeks is crucial as you have to vaccinate them with three shots. So, you can’t afford to miss vaccination schedule for dog and this is when you have to vaccinate them with DHPP, Parainfluenza, Rabies.
  • 1 year: This is the time for booster shots for DHPP, Parainfluenza and Rabies.
Age Core Vaccines Lifestyle Vaccines
6–8 weeks DAP* Bordetella Parainfluenza (often included in DA2PP combo vaccine)
10–12 weeks DHLPP Lyme Canine influenza
14–16 weeks DHLPP (vets prefer giving final DHLPP vaccine at 16 weeks or later) Rabies vaccine (may be given earlier if required by law) Lyme Canine influenza

 

Mandatory Vaccination Schedule for Adult Dogs in India

Now that your dog become an adult you have to follow proper dog shot schedule chart as it helps to maintain their immunity:

  • Every 1-3 years: When your dog age is between 1-3 years, you have to vaccinate them with DHPP, Parainfluenza, and Rabies booster shots.
  • Annually: After they have exceeded 3 years of age, you have to vaccinate them with Bordetella (kennel cough) and Leptospirosis vaccinations (if necessary).
Frequency Core Vaccines Lifestyle Vaccines
Annual vaccines for dogs Rabies (initial vaccine) Leptospirosis Lyme Canine influenza Bordetella (sometimes given every six months)
Dog vaccinations given every three years DAP Rabies (after initial vaccine, given every three years) No three-year lifestyle vaccines are available at this time

Which Dog Vaccines Does My Dog Need?

There are various points on which their vaccination is decided such as lifestyle, age and health status. However, it is really important to determine which vaccine does your dog requires. Here is the guide that will help you:

1- Core Vaccine: This vaccine is important for all of the dogs irrespective of their lifestyle or location. These vaccines are helpful to protect against DHPP, Rabies and Parainfluenza.

2- Non-Core Vaccines: This vaccine is recommended when dogs are at risk of contracting specific diseases. This vaccine is proven to fight against Bordetella, Leptospirosis and Lyme Disease.

3- Lifestyle based vaccine: As the name suggests, these vaccines are tailored as per your dog’s specific lifestyle and geographic location. This type of vaccine is designed to fight against diseases that are prevalent in your region or related to your dog’s activities such as :

  • Hiking: This vaccine is helpful to fight with Leptospirosis and Lyme disease.
  • Kenneling: This vaccine is helpful to prevent diseases like Bordetella and Parainfluenza.

You can consult with our expert veterinarian online who will suggest you the best dog vaccine schedules and specific shots as well. This will be properly based on their lifestyle, age and health status.

Veterans are expert to take a deep and detailed look at your dog’s health and lifestyle and other aspects. This helps to prepare the effective plan and specific dose for your dog. Don’t forget that a simple vaccine can help to save the life of your dog from a deadly disease.

Don’t Let Your Dog Suffer: The Importance of Vaccinations

Is your dog’s life at risk? Unvaccinated dogs are more vulnerable to deadly diseases like Parvovirus, distemper, rabies and vomiting in dogs caused by infections. If you miss any of the dog vaccination schedule India then deadly diseases can strike your dog at any time. They can even lead your dog to fight for their life. Don’t take the risk. Vaccinate them today and provide them important protection which they need to lead a healthy and long life.

At DeePet we offer dog vaccination services, we know the importance of your dog’s health and wellbeing. This is why we recommend regular vaccination for puppies but for this you need to understand key factors, vaccination cost and safety measures which helps to protect your furry friend. Stay updated to give your dog the best chance to a healthy life.

Factors to Keep in Mind While Dog Vaccinations

There are different points that you need to keep in mind while vaccinating your dog. Here are some of them:

  • Age and Health status: Puppies when they are in their initial age requires special attention with puppy vaccination schedule India which generally starts from 6-8 weeks. However, adult dogs require booster shots. Not only this but the dogs having weak immune system will require special consideration.
  • Lifestyle and Risk factors: Those dogs who socialize with other dogs or animals such as kennels or dog parks then they would require additional dog vaccination schedule.
  • Geographic location: Those dogs who are living in areas with high incidence of certain diseases such as Lyme disease then should be treated with additional vaccination.
  • Vaccine Type: There are various types of vaccine available for puppy vaccination schedule such as core vaccines (DHPP, Rabies, Parainfluenza) and non-core vaccines (Bordetella, Leptospirosis, Lyme disease).

How Do I Know My Dog Is Up To Date on Shots?

As a responsible pet parent, keeping a record of your dog’s vaccination schedule is very important, but somehow, if you forgot this or have adopted a new pet and don’t know what is the history of vaccinations, then you should contact a nearby vet in your area. They will run an antibody test and let you know whether your pet needs immediate shots or their vaccination process needs to start over.

Not only do vet doctors vaccinate your puppies, but they also provide a pet health certificate to keep your dog’s vaccination schedule up to date.

What is The Dog Vaccination Price in India?

There are several factors that dominate the cost of vaccination for dogs and as a pet parent you need to know them. These are the factors:

1- Location: one of the points that is very important for vaccination charges is location. However, the urban areas might be having higher charges.

2- Vaccine Type: Core vaccines are might be less expensive than non-core vaccines.

3- Veterinary Clinic: One of the things that make a difference in cost of vaccination is type of veterinary clinics or hospital shots for dogs that you choose.

4- At-home Vaccination: If you want a vet doctor to come to your home and vaccinate your canine companion, you will need to pay extra visiting charges. Therefore, at-home vaccinations cost a little more.

However, here is cost estimation for pet parent through which you can get an idea:

  • Puppy Vaccination might be ranging between Rs. 500 – Rs. 1,500.
  • Adult dog vaccination price will be between Rs. 350 – Rs. 800.
  • Booster shots are less expensive as they cost between Rs. 200 – Rs. 600.

How Safe Are Dog Vaccines?

Generally all dog vaccine is safe and effective to prevent your canine friend from deadly disease. But vaccine may cause severe side effects, like anaphylaxis, are extremely rare, occurring in approximately 1 in 30k to 40k vaccinated dogs. However, as similar to other medical treatments have some cons, these vaccines also had some risks and side effects.

1- Mild side effects: There are mild side effects of vaccine such as fever, vomiting and diarrhea and. These side effects are normal and they can be resolved on their own.

2- Serious side effects: There are some of the serious side effects of vaccine such as allergic reactions and autoimmune disorders. These are rare but can often occur.

3- Vaccine failure: This problem can occur when the vaccine is not administrated properly. However, this condition can also be arises when you have forgotten vaccination schedule of dogs and the furry friend has to go through compromised immune system.

At DeePet dog vaccination services we take every precaution which can ensure the safety and accuracy of the vaccinations. We have experienced and talented veterinarian who is there to guide you through the process and resolve any concerns you face.

Dog Vaccination Side Effects: What You Need to Know

Vaccination plays vital role to prevent your dog from deadly diseases they are more likely to cause side effects as well. However, these side effects can be mild or temporary. But, in rare cases they can be severe. This is why it important to be cautious about side effects of dog vaccination as it ensures their safety.

Common side effects: Common side effects consist of mild side effects, allergic reactions such as hives, itching and swelling. While there are some of the pets who might feel pain or get swelling at the injection site.

Rare but serious side effects: Rare side effects can consist Anaphylaxis. This is actually a severe and life threatening allergic reaction which requires immediate veterinary attention.

The other serious side effect is autoimmune disorders such as autoimmune hemolytic anemia. The other serious side effect is Seizures and neurological disorders. This consists of neurological disorders, such as meningitis, after receiving a vaccination.

What to do When Your Dog Experience Side Effects?

It is rare, but if you see your dog is having some kind of side effects then you need to immediately contact a veterinary doctor for help. They are expert to assess your dog’s condition and offer expert guidance on how to manage these side effects. While it is rare, your veteran can recommend for hospitalization or further treatment.

FAQ’s About Dog & Puppy Vaccination Schedule

Q. How often does my dog needs to be vaccinated?

Ans – Puppies are more vulnerable to deadly diseases and this is why they require frequent vaccination. While, adult dog requires vaccine once 1-3 years.

Q. How much dog vaccination in India cost?

Ans – The price of vaccination for dogs can be affected by several points such as their lifestyle, age or breed etc. However, the average price for vaccine starts from ₹1000 and it can go upto ₹4000 or more.

Q. How long does it take for vaccination to become effective?

Ans – Vaccination tends to become effective after 7-14 days of administration.

Q. What should I do if my dog experience severe vaccination reaction?

Ans – When you see that your dog is experiencing some vaccination reaction you immediately have to connect with expert veterans. They will book dog vaccination schedule for your dog and treat them efficiently.

Q. How many times do I need to Vaccinate my dog for Rabies?

Ans – You must vaccinate your puppy with rabies shots within 90 days and use booster shots annually for continuous protection.

Q. What is 7 in 1 vaccine?

Ans – The 7 in 1 vaccine is also known as 7-way puppy shot. This is a combination vaccine which offers protection against distemper, parvovirus, adenovirus, parainfluenza, coronavirus, leptospirosis, and bordetella (kennel cough). It is actually a combination of both core and non-core vaccines.

Q. Can i delay my dog’s vaccination?

Ans – Yes, you can delay it for a day or two but delaying it for long period of time can create major issues for your dog.

Q. Do dog vaccine expire?

Ans – Some of the core vaccines such as rabies, distemper, parvovirus, and hepatitis last around three years.

Dog vomiting is most a common and worried issues for every pet owner. Being a pet owner, most people often feel helpless when dog is vomiting without any warning. The retching and vomiting may cause panic, but it is in your power to act wisely once you know what could be the cause of such symptoms.

According to the American Kennel Club, occasional expelling may not signal a serious issue, but frequent or severe episodes can indicate underlying health problems that require prompt attention through professional veterinary services in Delhi, Noida, or Gurgaon and for quick support you can talk to a vet online from the comfort of your home.

The reason for expelling can be a mild upset stomach or an underlying acute illness that requires serious medical attention. When you know why your dog is vomiting, you can make a more informed decision about how to treat them and provide the most appropriate quality of care.

Before proceeding with the topic, it would be beneficial to understand how vomiting occurs in dogs as a result of stress, what distinguishes vomiting from regurgitation, the various types of dog emesis that can indicate different underlying conditions, and its treatment.

Table of Contents

  • What Is Dog Vomiting?
  • Types of Dog Vomit & What They Indicate
  • Common Reasons Dogs Throwing Up and What They Indicate
  • How Stress and Anxiety Can Cause Vomiting in Dogs
  • What Your Dog’s Emesis Reveals about Their Health

  • Vomiting vs. Regurgitation: Spot the Difference

What Is Dog Vomiting?

Dog vomiting types

Dog vomiting, also recognized as emesis, is a condition typical of pups where they start throwing up their stomach contents, mainly food or liquid they consumed. A few breeds may vomit yellow bile or throw up with traces of mucus or blood. The underlying health issues primarily determine the type of vomit.

However, in more severe vomiting episodes, your dog might start throwing up their intestinal contents, even feces, instead of their general body mechanism of passing them through bowel movement. Vomiting feces, although uncommon, is a sure sign that your dog is consuming fecal matter without you noticing. Furthermore, it is also a sign of more fatal aggravated conditions, such as an intestinal blockage. So, visiting a vet is the immediate approach that a responsible pet owner should make.

Types of Dog Vomit & What They Indicate

Types of dog vomit – what different colors mean & when to worry

Every dog is different, and so is their vomit! The texture and color of the dog’s fur can give a good clue to the internal issue the dog is facing, which can also help the vet quite a bit. Even the frequency of throwing up can help narrow down the diagnosis. Listed below are the different types of vomit a dog can produce, along with what they can signify.

1 Yellow Vomit

If a dog hasn’t eaten for a long time, it can result in yellow emesis. Dogs can also vomit yellow fluid when they expel a lot, or they suffer from reflux (GERD). If a dog has yellow vomit and is in good health, then mild cases can be monitored at home but persistent bile emesis may need pet vaccination review to avoid infections.

2 White, Foamy Vomit

White, foamy puke may be a sign of acid reflux in some dogs. If the episodes are infrequent, it may not be necessary to consult a veterinarian. However, if the dog continually expels foamy vomit with no other contents, or if it has a swollen stomach and appears to be in pain, it may indicate life-threatening bloat or gastric-dilatation-volvulus (GDV). In that case, you need a urgent help from a veterinary doctor in Gurgaon right away.

3 Clear, Liquid Vomit

Chronic, single-episode bouts of emesis need not concern a vet, unless they are accompanied by repeated or severe vomiting. If a dog, however, sits down and gulps excessive amounts of water, the result is usually foamy, clear vomit.

4 Mucusy, Slimy, or Moldy Vomit

Puke that appears as mucus, slime, or contains moldy substances can happen as a result of parasites, eating rotten foods or garbage, and drinking polluted water from sources like ponds or puddles with green algae. If you board your dog frequently then choose safe pet boarding service to eliminate these risks.

5 Bloody Vomit

If your canine has vomited blood, do not delay and take your dog to the vet immediately. Try to preserve a small quantity of the bloody vomit and take it with you to the vet consultation. This can help distinguish the possible reasons. Bloody emesis in dogs may be seen in various forms: bright red, gelatinous, or even like coffee grounds.

6 Brown Vomit

Brown vomit can be from digested kibble, feces, or blood from the lower intestines, which resembles coffee vomit. If your puppy shows signs of this type of stomach contents, please take your puppy to the vet clinic immediately.

7 Grassy Vomit

Sometimes dogs eat grass if they feel unwell. In any case, a single occurrence of grassy puke does not constitute a medical crisis. Some dogs eat grass because they are bored, their bodies crave more fiber, or they simply enjoy the taste or texture of the grass.

If you observe your canine consuming large portions of grass, especially if accompanied by foamy vomit or emesis with bile, it could indicate a more serious medical condition, which a veterinarian ought to assess.

Common Reasons Dogs Throwing Up and What They Indicate

Step by step guide: what to do if your dog vomits

Vomiting is not a typical disease, as it surfaces as a symptom that happens due to a chain of issues that might range from mild stomach disorders to severe illnesses. Understanding common causes can help you make an informed decision about when to monitor at home and when emergency pet care is necessary.

Dietary Indiscretion

Dogs are known as curious eaters and often tend to get into the garbage, non-food items, or spoiled food. This sort of indiscretion irritates the stomach, triggering puking. Although these mild cases often pass gradually, ingestion of bones, toxins, or foreign objects demands immediate vet consultation.

Food Sensitivities or Allergies

The more sensitive dogs will have an adverse reaction to chicken and beef. Puking that is accompanied by diarrhea or itchy skin. Resolving the trigger is important, through a vet-recommended diet, to fix the problem.

Gastrointestinal Obstruction

An increase in the volume of vomit, when something is swallowed that can cause a blockage, is almost guaranteed. Along with the puke, extreme abdominal pain, loss of appetite, and bloating can be signs. This is an urgent nuclear situation, not to be taken lightly, as it may require surgery.

Infections or Toxins

Severe expelling, accompanied by symptoms such as diarrhea, lethargy, or tremors, can be caused by parvovirus, certain bacterial infections, and poisoning from substances like chocolate, grapes, xylitol, and certain household cleaners. These events are preventable with timely dog vaccination at home (Delhi).

Some other causes might include:

  • Pancreatitis
  • Allergies
  • Dehydration
  • Colitis
  • Poisons
  • Kidney failure
  • Parasites
  • Bloat
  • Cancer
  • Abrupt changes in a dog’s diet

Dog emesis happens irrespective of dog breeds or age, and there is often an elevated risk in younger, unvaccinated pups that are exposed to contagious diseases or immunocompromised senior dogs.

How Stress and Anxiety Can Cause Vomiting in Dogs

Dogs not only experience mental pressure, but pressure also has a direct effect on their stomachs. Research shows that anxiety can alter gut motility and microbiota, leading to symptoms like nausea, diarrhea, or dog expelling white foam. Events such as loud noises, new environments, or long separations may trigger this response. Combining an anxious animal with a predictable environment and aid products, such as a calming collar, may be effective in reducing the frequency of episodes.

Routine enrichment may also help canine that have a history of anxiety, which can sometimes be linked to health concerns like gastrointestinal upset, prompting owners to wonder why my furry friend is vomiting. Natural stress relief can be achieved through puzzle toys, scent work games, and regular exercise. In the most extreme cases, the veterinarian can prescribe appropriate behavioural modification or anti-anxiety drugs that suit the needs of your tail wagging friend.

What Your Dog’s Emesis Reveals about Their Health

safe and unsafe foods for dogs with vomiting issue

An important piece of information that can be gained by observing your dog’s vomit is the cause of the issue. The contents, consistency, and colour are carefully selected to aid in assessing urgency and determining the most suitable care. If you’re thinking, “dog is vomiting and loose motion,” it’s crucial to evaluate these signs promptly to avoid serious complications.

Recognizing Patterns in White Foam Vomiting

In the case of dog is vomiting white foam, it can be the presence of weak stomach irritation or acid reflux. This typically occurs when the stomach has been empty for an extended period, resulting in a buildup of gastric juices. Why my dog is expelling white foam is a question many ask. White foam emesis can be considered a harmless symptom. Still, it may become a concern when repeated, and frequent throwing up can indicate a more serious health disorder, such as kennel cough, gastritis, or pancreatitis. Observation of the regularity and related concomitants allows determining whether the intervention of a veterinarian is required.

Understanding Yellow Vomit and Bile Issues

The presence of yellow bile in vomit is an indication of irritation in the small intestine or stomach. Bouts of yellow liquid vomiting could be a result of an emptied stomach, poor feeding schedules, or minor gastrointestinal upsets when pet is vomiting yellow liquid contents. Bile puke can be occasionally prevented by maintaining regular feeding schedules and consuming small, frequent meals. In cases of persistent emesis, a veterinarian should rule out the presence of conditions such as pancreatitis, inflammatory bowel disease, or liver disease.

When Vomiting Happens After Meals

A frequent complaint among dog owners is repeated emesis soon after feeding. When asking myself why my dog expels after eating, it will be due to eating too quickly, food allergies, or worse complications such as megaesophagus or blockages. Using slow-feeding bowls and limiting food intake can help alleviate vomiting after eating; however, it is essential to consult a specialist if ongoing symptoms persist. In some cases, dog is vomiting white foam becomes a related concern, often pointing to gastrointestinal distress or empty stomach issues that should not be overlooked.

Dealing With Vomiting and Loose Stools

The vomiting that occurs together with diarrhea is very concerning, as it is a symptom of general gastrointestinal distress. In the situation where pet is throwing up yellow foam and there is loose bowel at the same time, it is highly possible that to are dehydrated. The development of these symptoms can be caused by infections, parasites, or food poisoning, and immediate at home veterinary treatment is necessary to stabilise your pet’s health state.

Loss of Appetite Accompanied by Vomiting

A dog eating food after puking should not be neglected. It usually indicates that something is wrong with the dog when it vomits and does not eat during this period. Pet owners often wonder why my dog pukes after eating, as this could signal digestive disorders or food intolerances. When a dog has a tummy problem, they will automatically refuse to get near the food; however, when anorexia is persistent within a dog in addition to puking, there are severe problems such as kidney failure or internal obstruction. Inspection is crucial in the first veterinary assessment.

Blood in Vomit and Its Implications

Dog emesis blood is a serious warning sign in your dog, so you should always act immediately. Fresh blood coming out of the esophagus or stomach tends to be bright red, whereas old blood is dark and resembles the colour of coffee grounds. The possible causes include conditions like gastric ulcers, poisoning, or tumours.

Dehydration as a Complication of Expelling

Another neglected sign of danger of frequent vomiting is dehydration. When your pup starts losing vast amounts of electrolytes and fluid through puke, their body fails to maintain balance. The common signs of this condition are sunken eyes, fatigue, dry gums, and skin that fails to revive when lifted gently.

This condition can be prevented with small amounts of fresh water. This can help with the mild cases; however, severe dehydration often needs the treatment approach with vet fluids administered intravenously. Tracking their hydration status following their vomiting episode ensures you can identify the issue sooner and take preventative measures accordingly.

Seasonal Changes and Their Impact on Digestion

Changes in temperature and routine have a significant impact on the digestive health of your dog. A few pups often undergo stomach disorders, mainly during seasonal fluctuations. The episodes surface during the summer when heat stress leads to dehydration or the winter when less physical activity can shift your pup’s metabolism.

As reported by the VCA Animal Hospital, the seasonal adjustments in diet, exercise routines, and hydration play an integral part in helping prevent gastrointestinal disorders. Focusing on their water intake and establishing a consistent meal schedule can help alleviate such seasonal health issues.

Effective Treatments for Vomiting in Dogs

Dog vomiting treatment: home remedies vs when to visit a vet

When it comes to dogs, treatments for vomiting vary depending on the underlying reason, possible accompanying conditions, and the dog’s medical condition at the time of treatment. While some forms of vomiting can be tended to at home, dogs puking continuously or in severe pain need immediate medical assistance. Here’s the approaches that may work for you.

Withholding Food Temporarily

In cases of mild emesis with no pain, withholding food for 12-24 hours may aid in the stomach’s recovery. Puppies, and small dogs for that matter, may also have to be gallant fasting for a period of less than 12 hours to control blood sugar levels.

Hydration is Key

In case of severe vomiting, where the dog may end up getting dehydrated, encourage water drinking, offering ice, or electrolyte solutions prescribed only by a vet in Delhi.

Bland Diet Introduction

Diet control involves starting a corn-sensitive diet if the dog is corn-sensitive or gets stomach irritation from corn, to protect the dog’s stomach.

Probiotics and Digestive Support

Dogs that have been through undue stress or have taken a poor diet spend many hours with their body full of effluents, and their guts are unfit. They need to be in a healthy condition, and healing is possible by taking canine probiotics. These probiotics help a dog eliminate waste in the body. The owner does need to check with a veterinarian for the proper dosage.

Medication When Necessary

Some causes might refer to a veterinarian to diagnose and treat the animal(s) with anti-nausea medication, acid reducers, or stomach-protecting drugs. For pancreatitis or very acute cases of gastritis, more holistic care is generally required, such as advanced care for fluids, pain treatment, or modifications to the feeding recipe.

Address Underlying Causes

Vomiting resolves with treatment, but to get effective treatment, the underlying problem has to be solved. Such as removing:

  • Pieces of brushes or removing foreign objects, or indiscreet dietary indiscretion for parasite control.
  • Switching to hypoallergenic or prescription diets for cows and/or to treat sensitivities.
  • Infections with supervet and chronic conditions, including those with Supervisors of the vet clinic, infection control, etc.

Monitoring and Follow-Up

Vomiting misreported events, a pattern, external symptoms, and keeping notes aid your mid vet for more precise modifications and advancements in the treatment and detecting complications at early stages.

Important Note: Human medications should never be given to dogs without a veterinarian’s treatment plan. Over-the-counter antiemetic medications or anti-vomiting medications might be harmful and can result in death to canines so also consult with vet doctor. If you follow right dog & puppy vaccination schedule then you can easily avoid deadly disease.

Vomiting vs. Regurgitation: Spot the Difference

Vomiting is active, involving heaving and abdominal contractions, while regurgitation happens passively without warning. Knowing the difference helps vets pinpoint if the issue lies in the stomach or esophagus. According to Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine, accurately observing which one your dog experiences leads to faster, more effective pet vomiting treatment.

Pet owners can watch for clues, such as the presence of bile (common in vomiting) or undigested food in the shape of a tube (typical of regurgitation). Keeping a simple diary of episodes—including time, food consumed, and symptoms—can be invaluable for your veterinarian’s assessment.

Recognizing When Vomiting Is Serious

Knowing when to receive assistance is an important aspect that can be the difference between a minor issue and emergency healthcare. Warning signs include frequent puking, dog vomiting blood, extreme lethargy, bloating, or not willing to drink. Knowing when it is time to be concerned about dog emesis makes you ready to take the necessary and quick steps to protect your pet by taking vet doctor help.

When to Take the Help of a Veterinarian

As a pet parent you are worried when your tail wagging friend health is not good. However staying clam & relax will help you to determine when you need to seek vet help. Here are some guidelines that help to understand when to visit a veterinarian is must.

  • If your dog is vomiting continuously from last 24 to 36 hours then must need to contact a vet specialist ask for the treatment.
  • Blood in vomits need immediate medical assistance.
  • If your dog behavior is changed and having pain then you must need to call a vet.

Preventive Measures for a Healthy Dog

The first step towards the prevention of vomiting is possible through good habits:

  • Provide regular meals of good quality with no abrupt change
  • Store poisonous foods and incinerate household chemicals out of children’s & pet’s reach
  • Use garbage-secured containers to block access to garbage
  • Ensure slow-feeding recyclable bowls are used on dogs that have a history of food gulping
  • Book regular visits to the vet for health checkups

Being proactive can help limit the occurrence of dog vomiting reasons and allow your furry friend to live a happy and healthy life.

Signs of a Dogs Broken Leg

It is important to recognize the signs of a broken leg early to prevent complications. Some of the most common dog broken leg symptoms to look for include

Limping or Not Putting Weight on the Leg

A dog with a broken leg may not want to walk on it or will drag it behind them.

Swelling or Deformity

Visible swelling or an unnatural position in the leg may suggest a fracture.

Whimpering or Crying

Your dog might complain, particularly when you touch the sore spot.

Bruising or Bleeding

You might see noticeable bruising or bleeding in some severe injuries.

Reluctance to Move

A puppy with a broken leg may be reluctant to run, play, or participate in activities they usually love.

When dog fractured leg treatment is delayed, the condition can worsen and it becomes more difficult to treat a dog bone fracture.

Types of Dog Leg Fractures

Knowing what kind of fracture your dog has is critical so your veterinarian can develop the right treatment plan. Types of fractures include:

Simple Fracture

A clear slit with minimal injury to neighboring vessels.

Compound Fracture

When the bone breaks and moves, it pushes through the skin, increasing the risk of infection.

Comminuted Fracture

The bone is broken in several places, often needing surgical treatment.

Expert Veterinarian at DeePet Services will examine the severity of the injury to suggest which dog fracture treatment will work best with your pet.

Preventing Dog Leg Injuries

When it comes to your dogs health and mobility, prevention is always the best medicine. Though you cannot eliminate the risk of leg injuries, there are steps you can take to reduce the likelihood of them happening.

One easy way to mitigate risk is to supervise your dog while he is playing. Keep an extra close watch if they are playing in places with uneven surfaces, slippery spots or anything that could cause tripping or falling. Many accidents can be avoided through vigilance.

It is also good to have leash training in advance. A well trained dog is unlikely to move suddenly or pull hard during walks, reducing the chances of falling or hitting someone.

It is also important to make the home a safe space. Eliminate hazards like slick floors, knickknacks, or unstable furniture that could cause your dog to slip or injure themselves.

Finally, exercise in moderation and visit your vet regularly. Correct exercise strengthens bones and joints, and regular health checkups can detect problems before they result in injury.

Following these preventive measures can help keep your dog healthy, active, and injury free.

Immobilize the Leg

Keep the leg sound and intact with a splint or durable material to prevent additional damage.

Keep Your Dog Calm

Limit movement and comfort your dog to prevent stress and further injury.

Avoid Home Remedies

You may read some dog broken leg home treatment advice but it is always better to go with the experts.

The cause of a broken leg will determine how it is treated. Here are the main options:

Non Surgical Treatment

In the case of small fractures, veterinarians can cast or splint the bone to give it time to heal. Infractures or puppy bone fractures can often be treated using this option, since they tend to heal fast in puppies that are small to mature size.

Dog Broken Leg Surgery

Surgical intervention is often necessary for severe fractures like compound or comminuted ones. This consists of lining up the bone again and holding it in place with pins, screws, or plates. Surgery allows the body to heal correctly and avoid complications.

title: A Guide to Dog and Puppy Vaccination Price in India
excerpt: Dog and Puppy Vaccination Cost in India: A Comprehensive Guide Ensuring your fur buddy’s good health and well-being is not only your responsibility by compulsion as a pet owner but also your emotional responsibility to see your friend in good health. And your responsibility begins with a proper vaccination programme for your dog and puppy. […]
content:
Dog and Puppy Vaccination Cost in India: A Comprehensive Guide

Ensuring your fur buddy’s good health and well-being is not only your responsibility by compulsion as a pet owner but also your emotional responsibility to see your friend in good health.

And your responsibility begins with a proper vaccination programme for your dog and puppy. A thorough vaccination is important not only from a person’s point of view if he is bitten by a dog but also to keep your furry friend safe from various contagious and life-threatening diseases.

These entire vaccination programs for your dog and puppies need pragmatic care and approaches.

Indeed, there is a vaccination cost for the dog involved for the entire process, but as a dog owner, you also have plenty of options to choose from according to your budget for pet care.

In this guide, we will walk you through various dog and puppy vaccinations in India, including.

  • Types of vaccines
  • Vaccination schedules
  • Dog vaccination cost
  • Factors Affecting Dog Vaccine Price

Table of Contents

  • What Are Dog Vaccinations?
  • Types of Dog Vaccinations
  • Puppy Vaccination Schedule
  • Adult Dog Vaccination Schedule
  • Cost of Dog Vaccinations in India
  • Cost of Puppy Vaccination Package
  • Adult Dog Vaccination Package
  • Things that affect how much vaccines cost
  • How One Should Choose the Best Veterinary Doctor
  • Typical Stories and Truths Regarding Vaccines
  • Ready to administer vaccinations
  • Care After Getting a Vaccine
  • FAQ’s About Dog & Puppy Vaccination Cost in India

Here we go!

What Are Dog Vaccinations?

As a preventative step, vaccination shields individuals from contracting a wide range of infectious and dangerous illnesses. Your dog and puppy depend much on this.

The activation of the immune system—which generates antibodies against particular pathogens—depends critically on vaccination.

This increases your dog’s and puppy’s immunity as well as provides final disease prevention.

Types of Dog Vaccinations

Dog vaccines fall into two primary categories: core vaccines and non-core vaccines.

Core Vaccines

Core vaccines are vital for all dogs as they protect against widespread and severe diseases. These include:

Rabies

A fatal disease affecting the central nervous system (CNS) of mammals, including humans. The rabies vaccine is mandatory in India and administered annually. Dog rabies vaccine prices in India remain competitive and it should be around Rs. 600 approx.

Canine Distemper Virus (CDV)

A highly contagious viral disease affecting the respiratory, gastrointestinal, and nervous systems. This vaccine is usually part of a combination shot given to puppies and this will cost you Rs. 800.

Canine Parvovirus (CPV)

A severe virus that causes acute gastrointestinal illness, primarily affecting puppies. The vaccine also protects against the CPV2c variant. Approx charges of parvovirus in India are around Rs. 800 per shots.

Canine Adenovirus (CAV-2)

Causes infectious canine hepatitis and respiratory diseases. Veterinarians often combine this vaccine with distemper and parvovirus vaccines. This vaccine is part of 9 in 1 dog vaccination combo and cost you Rs. 750.

Canine Parainfluenza Virus

Contributes to kennel cough, a highly contagious respiratory disease. This vaccine is usually part of a combination vaccine 5 in 1 for dogs and its costing is Rs. 600.

Leptospirosis

A core vaccine that protects against the bacterial infection caused by several serovars, including:

  • Leptospira canicola: Commonly affects dogs.
  • Lepto icterohaemorrhagiae: Can cause severe illness in dogs.
  • Lepto grippotyphosa: Often found in raccoons and opossums.
  • Lepto Pomona: Commonly affects cattle and swine but can also infect dogs.

Explanation

Vaccine Details

The leptospirosis vaccine is an inactivated bacterin purified to reduce adverse reactions. The Zoetis Lepto vaccine (Vanguard L4) effectively protects against all four serovars. The veterinarians can administer it to puppies as young as six weeks.

Multivalent Protection

The DHPPi-L vaccine protects against Canicola, Icterohaemorrhagiae, Grippotyphosa, and Copenhagen serovars. The price for this vaccine is Rs. 600 per dose and this will also include in combination of 7 in 1 vaccine for dogs.

Health Advisory

The American College of Veterinary Internal Medicine (ACVIM) recommends this vaccine.

Signs of Leptospirosis in Dogs:

  • Muscle pain, stiffness, or trembling
  • Reluctance to move
  • Bleeding disorders
  • Cough or breathing difficulties
  • Uveitis (inflammation of the eye)

Non-Core Vaccines

Non-core vaccines are based on a dog’s lifestyle and risk factors. These include:

Bordetella bronchiseptica: A primary cause of kennel cough, essential for dogs that frequently interact with others. The rate of bordetella bronchiseptica vaccine is Rs. 1000 approx.

Lyme Disease

Transmitted through tick bites, this vaccine is advised for dogs in tick-prone areas.

Canine Influenza

A respiratory infection that spreads quickly in social settings like kennels and dog parks.

Puppy Vaccination Schedule

Puppies need a series of vaccinations to build robust immunity. Here’s a typical puppy vaccination schedule in India:

  • 6-8 Weeks: First dose of DHPPi (Distemper, Hepatitis, Parvovirus, Parainfluenza), Leptospirosis, and Bordetella.
  • 10-12 Weeks: Second dose of DHPPi and Bordetella.
  • 14-16 Weeks: Third dose of DHPPi and the first dose of Rabies.
  • 12-18 Months: Booster shots for DHPPi, Rabies, and Leptospirosis.

Adult Dog Vaccination Schedule

To maintain immunity, adult dogs also need regular vaccinations:

  • Annually: Rabies, DHPPi, and Leptospirosis.
  • Every 1-3 Years: DHPPi booster shots.

Cost of Dog Vaccinations in India

The cost of dog vaccinations varies based on the type of vaccine and the veterinary doctor. Approximate costs include:

Vaccine Approximate Cost (INR)
Rabies 600
DHPPi 800
Leptospirosis 800
Bordetella 1000
Lyme Disease 400
Canine Influenza 400

Cost of Puppy Vaccination Package

The price for the puppy vaccination combo is Rs. 5,999 per session, which includes a set of multiple vaccines:

  • 35th day Puupy DP
  • 50th day DHPPiL
  • 60th day Canine Corona
  • 71st day DHPPil (Booster)
  • 90th day Canine Corona (Booster)
  • 90th day Anti Rabies
  • 120th day Anti Rabies (Booster)
  • 120th day Kennel Cough
  • Deworming

Adult Dog Vaccination Package

Cost of Adult dog vaccination combo is Rs. 2799 and it includes:

  • Anti-Rabies
  • DHPPiL
  • Canine Corona
  • Kennel Cough
  • Deworming

Things that affect how much vaccines cost

Several things can affect how much dog vaccines cost, such as

  • Place: Veterinary hospitals in cities may charge more than those in the country.
  • How the clinic is known: Clinics that are well-known and have experienced vets may charge more.
  • Extra Services: Some clinics give extra services, like health checks and consultations, that can make the total cost go up.

How One Should Choose the Best Veterinary Doctor

The health of your dog depends much on the veterinary doctor you choose to trust. These ideas should help you decide on the suitable course of action:

  • See comments and recommendations from pet owners already.
  • To find out how tidy the clinic is and the staff member’s skill level, visit it.
  • Ask the veterinarian about their credentials, experience, and offered services without hesitation.
  • Cost is crucial; find a facility paying a reasonable fee for competent treatment.

You can check this guide on how to find trusted vet doctor for pets.

Typical Stories and Truths Regarding Vaccines

Though they are a necessary component of pet health care, immunisations are surrounded by many myths and erroneous ideas. Some well-known stories have to be refuted:

One fallacy holds that immunisations cause illness.

  • Vaccines are supposed to prevent illness, not cause it in anyone. Though these side effects—such as tiredness or fever—some dogs may experience small ones, but often, these effects are not severe.
  • Second myth: indoor dogs require no vaccinations.
  • Dogs housed indoors can also become sick from running across other animals, people, or the outdoors. A dog needs vaccinations regardless of their type of living.
  • Dogs immunised once do not require boosters.
  • Maintaining high immunity over time depends on getting booster shots. Your dog may become sick more likely if you skip boosters.

Ready to administer vaccinations

A few simple actions will ensure that receiving your dog vaccinated goes without any complications and any anxiety:

  • Arranging a Vet Visit: See your doctor to prevent waiting a lot of time.
  • Deactivate medical records: Bring any medical documents and immunological records you own.
  • Peaceful environment: Try everything to relax your dog before the conference. One can benefit from a game or a walk.
  • Stay with your dog: This will enable them to develop confidence and feel better during their vaccinations.

Care After Getting a Vaccine

After getting your puppy vaccinated, you should keep an eye on them for any side effects and give them the right care:

  • Keep an eye on reactions: Watch out for any bad responses, like swelling, throwing up, or having trouble breathing. If you see any signs that worry you, call your vet.
  • Give comfort: After getting the shot, your dog might feel a little tired or sore. Give them lots of water and a nice place to rest.
  • Don’t do anything too hard: Don’t let your dog do much for 24 hours after getting a shot to help it heal.

FAQ’s About Dog & Puppy Vaccination Cost in India

Q. What is 9 in 1 vaccine price for dogs in India?

Ans – The 9-in-1 vaccine combines nine different vaccines, including canine distemper, adenovirus, leptospirosis, canine parvovirus (CPV), Puppy DP/DHPPi, canine adenovirus type 2, coronaviral enteritis, Leptospira pomona, and Leptospira grippotyphosa. This injection costs Rs. 800 in India and should be administered to puppies aged 6 to 8 weeks.

Q. What is the cost of rabies vaccination for dogs?

Ans – The approximate cost of an anti-rabies injection for dogs is around Rs. 600 in India.

Q. Which is the most and least expensive puppy shot?

Ans – The most expensive puppy vaccination is kennel cough, which costs Rs. 1,000, while the anti-rabies vaccine is the least expensive, at Rs. 600.

Q. How much does it cost for a dog’s 1st vaccine?

Ans – The first injection you need to give your dog is the Puppy DP vaccine, which costs Rs. 1000.

Q. What is the price of the 7-in-1 injection, and which vaccines does this combination include?

Ans – The cost of the 7-in-1 vaccine in India is approximately Rs. 800. This vaccine includes canine distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, canine adenovirus type 2, parainfluenza, parvovirus (CPV), and leptospira strains.

Q. Vaccines last what length of time?

Ans – Vaccines don’t shield you immediately. The immune system needs time to identify the vaccination and create a defence following its administration. Usually, the vaccination fights against sickness and stimulates the immune system to function better between a few days and many weeks. Puppy’s first vaccinations cause immunity to develop gradually over several doses. For a long period, booster doses help maintain immunity high, therefore shielding the puppy against infections.

Q. Are there any bad effects that come from vaccinating dogs?

Ans – Vaccines are generally well tolerated by dogs, but some may have mild side effects. These are some common side effects:

Your dog might be tired or less busy for one or two days.
A mild fever is a normal immune reaction that causes the body’s temperature to rise a little.
Localised swelling: Some dogs may get a small lump where they were injected, but it generally goes away in a few days.
Dogs may eat less than normal for a short time if they aren’t feeling well.

Sometimes, very bad responses can happen, like

Having diarrhoea or vomiting
Getting a big face or legs
Having trouble breathing
Giving up or being very weak

Please call your vet right away if your dog has any serious reactions. These side effects are very uncommon, and the benefits of getting vaccinated are much greater than the risks.

Q. Can I try something with my dog right here at home?

Ans – You should not try to immunize your dog at home. Your dog should instead be seen by a licensed veterinarian. Veterinary clinics are aware of how to administer sensible and efficient vaccines. They have the necessary tools, spotless rooms, and understanding to do so. Before injecting your dog, the veterinarian will also examine her health.

Make sure you understand how to provide the correct dosage.

Plan your treatment both following a vaccination and when to get a booster dose.

Spot and address any negative reactions immediately.

Q. Should my dog not get an extra vaccine, what should I do?

Ans – Should your dog miss an extra shot, relax. Usually, the schedule can be brought back up to the current since the immune system recalls some aspects of the last shot. The type of vaccination you receive and the length of time since your last shot will determine whether and when you require a further one.

You ought to do this:

Share it with your veterinarian: They will ask whether you can maintain giving your dog the same daily dosage or whether it needs an additional one.
Wait hardly too long: Some vaccines, including the rabies shot, have tight guidelines and may have to be given once more should they be ignored for too long.
Keep to your vaccination regimen: Maintaining your dog’s safety from avoidable ailments depends on your maintenance of notes and records.

Conclusion

Ensuring your dog receives the correct vaccinations is quite crucial for any decent pet owner. By timing your pet’s vaccinations to coincide with them, one should be aware of their expenses. Choose a trustworthy veterinary doctor in Gurgaon—you can help to maintain your pet free of ailments and in good condition. Vaccines ensure your pet’s health. By halting the transmission of diseases, they also contribute to maintaining public health.

Vaccinating your dog will help to long-term invest in their health and well-being. Your pet’s quality of life will improve if you routinely visit the veterinarian and follow the immunisation schedule. Recall that a lucky dog is a healthy dog and that getting vaccinated is mostly responsible for that.

How to Get a Veterinary Health Certificate for Traveling Animals

Get a Veterinary Health Certificate +91 7500367400

Having your pet accompany you during travel is exciting, but it needs to be prepared for.

One of the most crucial things you need to get is a travel pet health certificate. It confirms that your pet is healthy enough for travel.

If you do not have this document, your pet will not be allowed to enter the city that you are heading to.

Below is a step-by-step guide on how to get a travel pet health certificate and why you should get one. You can directly contact DeePet Services at 7500367400 to generate a valid pet health certificate.

Table of Contents

  • Why You Should Get a Pet Health Certificate When Traveling
  • How to Obtain a Pet Health Certificate for Travel
  • Can Pet Health Certificates Be Obtained Online?
  • How Much Does a Dog Health Certificate Cost

Why You Should Get a Pet Health Certificate When Traveling

You have to get a pet health certificate for travel to make your pet disease-free and safe to travel.

It is compulsory in some countries before it can be accepted. It is to make other animals and human live disease-free. It also makes your pet fit for travel.

Having a domestic pet travel certificate guarantees that your pet will not have any issues entering the destination city. It guarantees that your pet is healthy and has been vaccinated as needed.

How to Obtain a Pet Health Certificate for Travel

Obtaining a pet certificate of health is simple. This is what you should do:

1. Consult a Veterinarian

First consult with an accredited veterinarian. Examination of the pet will be performed to check the health status of the animal for travel. If the pet is sick, treatment may be recommended before traveling. Health certificates for travel cannot be issued except by a licensed veterinarian.

2. Verify Vaccinations Are Up to Date

One of the main purposes of a dog health certificate for travel is to ensure your dog is current with all of their shots they need. A perfect example would be rabies, which most nations require. Your vet will figure out if your dog is current with all the shots that they need. In the event your dog is not current, your vet will give them shots for those and then issue the certificate.

3. Health Check

The veterinarian in Delhi will perform a thorough check-up of your pet. The veterinarian will examine the eyes, ears, teeth, and general health of your pet. If everything is fine, the veterinarian will give a travel pet health certificate. If there is any issue, the veterinarian will prescribe medicine prior to traveling.

4. Get the Health Certificate

Once you are done with your check-up, your veterinarian will let you out with the pet health certificate for travel. It may either be offered in print form or veterinary health certificate pdf India. You can simply print and bring along the certificate.

5. Verify Travel Requirements

Different countries have different regulations for taking pets along. It is worth it to know what that target country needs. The country might need something more than the dog health certificate for travel in India. They might need an international health certificate for dogs or additional testing.

Can Pet Health Certificates Be Obtained Online?

Yes, in some cases, you can even get a pet health certificate for travel online.

We at DeePet Services offer online facilities where you fill in your pet’s information such as dog name, age, breed, and we will issue the certificate. Just ensure that the online certificate is acceptable at the destination city. Always check with the vet beforehand before using it for travel.

How Much Does a Dog Health Certificate Cost:

The price of a dog health certificate may be varied. It may be INR 700 to INR 2,500 in India. The vet charges according to the vet, the vaccination needed, and the tests to be performed.

You may also be charged extra for other tests such as pet vaccinations cost or further health checks costs. Get the total cost from your vet in advance to prevent any surprise.

What to Include in the Pet Health Certificate

There will be vital pieces of information on a pet health certificate pdf.

Such information includes:

  • Details of Pet: Its name, age and breed are followed by an identification number (such as a microchip).
  • Vaccination History: Shows all vaccinations that the pet had, most importantly rabies.
  • Health Status: Should indicate that the pet is healthy and free from diseases, and fit to travel.
  • Veterinarian Information: Name of the veterinarian, contact number and signature.

Advantages of Travel with a Pet Health Certificate

You need a pet health certificate for the below reasons:

  • Legal Entry: It makes your pet legally eligible for entry into the country.
  • Quarantine Avoidance: Without it, your pet would end up in quarantine. It tends to delay the travel.
  • Assurance of Good Health: It ensures that your pet is good for travel. It ensures good health of the pet.
  • Peace of Mind: With all this in order, travel is seamless and easy.

What if the Pet Does Not Have a Health Certificate?

Without a pet health certificate to travel, your dog will be refused entry into the country of destination.

Your dog will be quarantined in other countries, and other countries will refuse your dog entry.

In order not to leave all this behind from occurring, make sure you get the health certificate of the dog before leaving. But due to some reasons you are not able to take your pet with you then you can leave your pet to our boarding center in Gurgaon.

Proper documents will give you a smooth and timely ride for your dog. Veterinary health certificate for dogs in very necessary.

Things to Keep in Mind

  • Be Prompt: It is going to take time to produce the health certificate. Plan early so that your pet travels in a systematic manner.
  • Verify Rules to Your Destination: Pet traveling rules differ in each city & country. Always check the requirements prior to initiating the procedure.
  • One Certificate per One Animal: Each pet must have one health certificate. One certificate could not be issued for more than one pet.
  • The Certificate Must Be Signed by a Qualified Veterinarian: A certificate of health for a dog must be signed only by a licensed vet. Make sure you do visit a qualified vet. You can contact us to for at home vet visit in Noida to generate health certificate for your furry friend.

Conclusion

Pet travel health certificate is a highly critical part of preparing to travel with your pet in India. It is an easy process but needs to be carried out carefully. When you make your pet travel ready, vaccinate, and healthy, you will avoid trouble reaching the destination.

Be sure to visit an authorized veterinarian, check the rules for travel for your destination, and obtain required paperwork. Doing this will make your pet a safe and relaxed journey.

FAQ’s About Pet Health Certificate for Travel in India

Q. How long does a pet health certificate remain valid?

Ans – A pet health certificate typically remains valid for 7 to 10 days. Some nations accept 30-day-old certificates. Be sure to get an update on what they require from the destination.

Q. Is it possible to purchase a pet health certificate online?

Ans – Yes, sometimes you can get a pet health certificate for travel through the internet. But ensure that an online certificate that is recognized by the destination country is being offered.

Q. How much does one have to pay in order to get a pet health certificate?

Ans – A dog travel health certificate in India will cost anywhere from INR 500 to INR 2,500. It will vary depending on the veterinarian and what your pet requires, such as vaccination or testing.

It is simple to get a pet health certificate, but it really does make a difference. With the proper paperwork, your pet will be good to go, and you can avoid hassle in between.

content:
The dogs are valuable pets that people adore and appreciate for their loyal, loving, and protective nature. However, not every breed is suitable in all settings, particularly in a crowded nation like India. Some breeds, due to their size, temperament, and aggressive tendencies, have been deemed unsafe to live in towns and cities, and they are currently subject to numerous legislative restrictions and city policies.

This awareness of these bans is essential for people who already own dogs or plan to acquire them in the future so that they can make responsible, well-informed decisions. This guide describes these breeds and reasons why they are banned, and also outlines safety issues and which are the banned dog breeds in India?

Table of Contents

  • Banned Dogs in India: How These Canines Ended Up on the List
  • Why Did Indian Government Banned These Dog Breeds?
  • Safe Alternative: Popular Legal Dog Breeds in India
  • Responsible Dog Ownership With DeePet
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Banned Dogs in India: How These Canines Ended Up on the List

To understand the dangerous dog breeds banned in India, it is essential to comprehend the reasons, primarily due to their aggressive nature, strong physical characteristics, and difficulties in responsible rearing. We will discuss these breeds, their history, and the rationale of inclusion in the list of banned dogs in India below.

Pitbull Terrier

Pit Bull terriers are strong, persistent, and have a somewhat controversial image worldwide. This breed was historically raised for bull-baiting and then for dog fighting, and as a result, has enormous strength and tenacity. Leaving Pitbulls in irresponsible hands may make them unpredictable, and hence, they are a risky type of dog in a congested area. It requires a profound understanding of canine psychology to control these dogs safely for their owners.

The government of India has acted out of caution to safeguard the communities by limiting the ownership of Pitbulls. Is Pitbull banned in India? Various states have included this breed on their list of restricted or prohibited dogs to check for possible threats. Records show that despite the aggressive insistence of Pit Bull breed lovers that the breed does not deserve the ban because it is being misunderstood, the ban is focused on the safety of the people rather than engaging in an argument.

Rottweiler

Rottweilers are known to be protective, intelligent, and very loyal dog breeds, making them good guard dogs. Nonetheless, the same aspects may become harmful without strong leadership and strict training. They possess strong bodies and strong bites, so even a slight lapse in discipline might escalate into serious, unacceptable cases.

Is the Rottweiler banned in India?

Yes, this breed appears on the list of dogs prohibited in several Indian states due to reported attacks and the inability to control them in densely populated areas. The critics say that there are ways how which responsible ownership can help to reduce these risks, but the existing laws are rather cautious.

Japanese Tosa

The Japanese Tosa is a large, dignified breed that was bred for fighting in Japan. A calm breed, the Tosa is nevertheless extremely powerful and protective when needed, which can prove unreliable in a family-oriented environment. Its threatening nature can cause tension among neighbors and commoners.

The fact that this breed is on the list of prohibited dog breeds is a global trend, as numerous countries have similar bans in place. Indian leaders believe that Tosas require spaces and state-of-the-art training facilities, which are often unavailable in big cities, to understand the number of dogs banned in India. As a result, ownership has been widely prohibited.

Dogo Argentino

In Argentina, Dogos were bred to hunt large game, such as pumas and wild boars. The breed is energetic, has a good prey drive, and a muscular body that requires excessive exercise and a professional guide. Without these, behavioural problems may surface.

This aspect of their physical strength, combined with a desire to protect, has led to a few cases of aggression being witnessed around the world. Being aware of such risks, India has also included the Dogo Argentino in the list of banned dogs to prevent accidents in crowded residential areas.

Boerboel

Boerboels originated in South Africa, where they were raised as homestead and livestock guarders. These massive canines are not afraid of anything, very loyal, and always distant from strangers by nature. Boerboels are loyal towards their families; however, they may be overprotective when living in urban areas where strangers are a common thing.

They are very big and dominant enough to scare even skilled handlers. Governmental controls have placed Boerboels one of the most dangerous dog breed because they were intended to protect people in towns and cities that are not yet fully equipped financially and technically to handle such powerful breeds.

Wolf Hybrid

Wolf hybrids are the result of crossing wolves and domestic dogs, creating animals with unpredictable temperaments and instincts. Wolf hybrids tend to retain the wild characteristics of the wolf, such as a strong prey drive and fear-induced aggression, which may not be conducive to most homes, unlike other fully domesticated breeds.

The consideration of wolf hybrids in the list of dogs prohibited in India highlights the importance of both the safety and welfare of animals and people. Such creatures require extremely controlled conditions, and in Indian cities, that is not easily possible. Many dog owners of this breed love to give dangerous dog names to their pets according to their nature and size.

Fila Brasileiro (Brazilian Mastiff)

The Fila Brasileiro is a very loyal breed, characterised by strong protective instincts that can sometimes lead to aggression towards unfamiliar individuals. Bred originally in Brazil to stake and track down large prey, their size and strength can prove overbearing to inexperienced owners.

The wild nature of this breed in terms of behaviour around strangers has threatened the ownership of this breed in many countries, including India. This restricted dog breeds is intended to prevent accidents resulting from inadequate training and socialisation.

Presa Canario

The Presa Canario (Canary Mastiff) is a mastiff-type working dog originating in the Canary Islands. These breeds of dogs were traditionally employed as farm guards and livestock managers, but due to their size and physical power, they have also posed a menace to untrained people.

The Indian authorities considered urban conditions to be unsuitable for such a dominant breed. This has led to Presa Canarios being named as prohibited dog breeds to mitigate risks in a crowded environment.

American Bulldog

American Bulldogs are athletic and fierce, with strong protective tendencies that can become a problem if they are not socialised at an early age. They are affectionate with relatives but require owners who can train them regularly and accept their natural leadership tendencies.

This breed is restricted by Indian municipalities, which are concerned with public safety. The fact that they are among the 10 banned dog breeds in India indicates that an effort has been made to prevent the occurrence of preventable episodes in both urban and rural populations.

Kangal

Kangal is a giant livestock guardian dog originating from Turkey, characterised by a fearless nature and protective behaviour, but one of the top 10 restricted dog breeds. They grow large and are strong, which enables them to face large predators. However, this breed is extremely disadvantageous in an urban Indian setting where space and safe confinement are restricted.

The intimidating ability and force of this breed to bite have led to it being included on a list of breeds banned in India. To handle a Kangal safely, owners require a significant amount of resources and expertise.

Cane Corso

Cane Corsos are Italian Mastiffs that serve as large police guard dogs, protecting property and also hunting big game. They have an inappropriate muscle physique and territorial traits, which do not suit first-time owners in urban Indian settings.

Without socialisation at an early age and frequent training, the protective instinct and the power of this breed may lead to the development of aggression. Cane Corsos are also restricted dog breeds by authorities, which may also pose some safety issues in densely populated areas where they may find it difficult to restrain such a powerful dog.

Why Did Indian Government Banned These Dog Breeds?

The decision to ban these dog breeds are for public safety. In the recent years India has witnessed a sharp rise of fatal dog attacks, especially involving children’s, ladies & elderly peoples.

The main reason are:

  • Dog Bites: According to Times of India & The Hindu around 37 lakhs dog bite cases reported in 2024.
  • Rabies Death: 54 deaths are reported due to rabies in 2024.
  • Recent Surge: Dog bite cases increased significantly from 2.18 million in 2022 to over 3.7 million in 2024.
  • Recent Stats: The country witnesses around 10k dog bites every day.

Safe Alternative: Popular Legal Dog Breeds in India

If you are planning to adopt a family friendly dog breeds then here is the alternative options for you:

  • Golden Retriever: Good looking & intelligent, great option for first time owners.
  • Labrador Retriever: Safe, trusted, loyal, and perfect for kids.
  • Shih Tzu of Pug: Small size dog well suitable for single parents and urban households.
  • Beagle: Energetic, and social pet easily adapt the apartment life.
  • India Pariah (Indie Dogs): High adaptability, low maintenance, and perfect for Indian conditions.

Responsible Dog Ownership With DeePet

A dog is a long-term companion, and you are taking both a moral and a proactive responsibility for their well-being, safety, and training. Some of the breeds, particularly those on the country’s ban lists in India, require exceptional resources and specialised expertise to be handled responsibly.

At DeePet Services, we are firm believers that every pet should have a happy place to live and a loving family to call their own that suits their interests. So for any type of pet care services call us anytime.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q. Is Pitbull banned in India?

Ans – Yes Pit Bull are banned in India. You are not allowed to import or breeding. Existing owner face restrictions.

Q. Is German Shepherd banned in India?

Ans – No German Shepherd are not restricted and they are one the most safest pet breed in India because of it’s friendly behaviour.

Q. Which dogs are banned in India?

Ans – 1. Cane Corso
2. Pitbull Terriers
3. Rottweiler
4. Japanese Tosa
5. Wolf Hybrid
6. Dogo Argentino
7. Boerboel
8. Brazilian Mastiff
9. Presa Canario
10. American Bulldogs
11. Kangal

Q. Why Tibetan Mastiff banned in India?

Ans – The Tibetan Mastiff is marked as dangerous and fighting dog, with records of aggression worldwide. Its strength and behavior make it unsuitable for Indian families.

Q. Are there special permissions to keep banned dog restricted in India?

Ans – There are no exceptions to the ban on banned breeds in the majority of Indian states. Even special permission is rarely allowed to ensure the safety of the population and to avoid legal responsibility to the owners.

Q. In the case of prohibited dog breeds, are they euthanised upon discovery in India?

Ans – Authorities generally avoid euthanasia. Dogs that have been confiscated as banned are rehomed in safer places, taken to shelters, or kept under tight supervision, depending on municipal policies and a court order.

Q. Can an illegal dog breed be transformed into a safe type in India?

Ans – Even with excellent dog training, banned breeds remain restricted legally. The safety issues are related to intrinsic factors, such as size and power, which the training process cannot eradicate under urban living conditions.
